title: Signal Fusion RICE+ for OKR-driven roadmap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Proposal for a reproducible, time-aware prioritization framework that fuses traditional RICE scoring with explicit cost and latency impact signals and OKR alignment weights. The goal is to surface work that optimizes product outcomes (OKRs) while keeping inference unit economics and SLOs within acceptable bounds. This ticket defines the scoring model, decision rules, evaluation plan, and rollout steps for migrating roadmap reviews to the new signal-fusion rubric.
scoring_model_details:
High-level formula (human-readable): CompositeScore = WeightedSum(RICE_base_score, CostImpactScore, LatencyImpactScore, OKRAlignmentScore, ConfidenceMultiplier, DecayFactor).
- RICE_base_score: standard Reach * Impact / Effort normalized to 0-100.
- CostImpactScore: expected change in $/1k tokens (signed), mapped to a 0-100 penalty/bonus scale.
- LatencyImpactScore: expected p95 ms delta, mapped to a 0-100 penalty scale with steeper slope near SLO breach.
- OKRAlignmentScore: explicit alignment weight (0-100) from product leads per quarter.
- ConfidenceMultiplier: 0.5-1.2 scale based on data confidence and prototype signals.
- DecayFactor: exponential time decay (quarter half-life) to reduce priority of stale requests.
Note: All sub-scores are z-normalized within the candidate pool each cycle to avoid absolute scale mismatches.
decision_rules:
1) Any candidate with LatencyImpactScore indicating >10% risk of SLO breach is flagged for architecture review and gets an automatic hold until mitigation plan is provided.
2) If CompositeScore difference between two items < 5 points, prefer the one with higher OKRAlignmentScore.
3) Customer-facing P0 bugs override CompositeScore and are slotted into next sprint.
4) Projects with ConfidenceMultiplier < 0.7 require a 2-week spike before being accepted.
5) Final prioritization is decoupled from exact dollar estimates; the model surfaces trade-offs, PMs still set trade-priorities during roadmap cadence.
metrics: Primary: fraction of roadmap work aligned to top-3 OKR outcomes (target >= 70%), median CompositeScore delta pre/post adoption, mean token-cost per 1000 generated tokens for prioritized features, distribution of p95 latency changes for shipped items. Secondary: number of hold events due to SLO risk, proportion of items with ConfidenceMultiplier <0.8 that eventually ship within 2 cycles.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot, 2 cycles): apply model to 20 candidate items in Growth and Infra initiatives; collect feedback from PMs and Eng. Phase 1 (adopt for roadmap review): update intake form, require cost/latency estimates on all new tickets, train product & eng on score interpretation. Phase 2 (automation): add calculator to roadmap spreadsheet and integrate with console dashboards to pull p95 baselines and cost estimates. Phase 3 (enforcement): link to release gating - items flagged for SLO risk must attach mitigation PR before merge. Timeline: pilot complete by 2026-03-31, platform integration by 2026-06-15.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prioritization rubric documented and reviewed by at least 3 PMs and 2 Eng leads.
- Pilot run completed with 20 items and annotated scores available.
- Dashboard prototype shows CompositeScore for each candidate and underlying signals.
- At least one roadmap decision during pilot used the composite score and logged rationale.
- Feedback captured and at least 3 improvements scheduled for next cycle.
notes: Key trade-offs: increasing OKRAlignment weight biases toward product bets that may raise unit cost; adding cost signal helps compensate but requires reasonable cost estimation discipline. Need to avoid overfitting the rubric to short-term incentives. Consider quarterly re-calibration of z-normalization buckets to keep scores stable across changing candidate pools.
